parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, facility ban, border or police targeting of trans people is documented; bathroom access, anti-discrimination and hate-crime protection covering gender identity are in force, with reporting routes and an equality complaints body. That places this above jurisdictions with only friction or uneven remedies. It sits below the 0.85-0.95 anchors because traveller-specific enforcement outcomes, custody/ward placement and foreign-document practice are not documented, hate crimes are rising in small non-disaggregated counts, and acknowledged protection gaps are unspecified. Resident self-ID and family law are treated only as institutional-climate signals.

entry_documents.interaction: Domestic X-marker availability does not establish acceptance of foreign passports; no border mismatch practice is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No detention, search or placement rule for trans visitors is documented, so no combined-regime interaction can be rated.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom or public-facility exclusion is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Bathroom access is documented as protected, and discrimination is illegal nationally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National protections apply with no documented regional difference; outside the capital there is sparse gay scene, not a documented facility restriction.

care_services.interaction: No documented ward, emergency-care or medication rule for trans visitors; intersex and conversion-therapy laws are resident-facing climate signals only.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence or state threat-framing is documented; a queer group calls for stronger hate-crime legislation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime and anti-discrimination law covers gender identity; same-sex activity is legal nationwide.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Progressive legal trajectory and visible pride support a non-hostile state climate, but unspecified acknowledged gaps limit certainty.

minors_guardians.exposure: No traveller-facing restriction on a minor or guardian is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident minors may change legal gender with parental consent; this does not establish visitor care, school or document treatment for foreign minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police-recorded potential hate crimes were 16 in 2023, 11 in 2024 and 7 year-to-date, but counts are small and not disaggregated by target group.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National emergency guidance defines hate crime, notes queer people face higher victimisation risk, and provides reporting routes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts do not establish a trans-specific violence rate; no pattern of police non-response or targeting is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Acknowledged gaps in protection are mentioned without specification.
remedies_unknowns.protection: An official equality complaints body and victim reporting routes exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy existence is documented, but no traveller case outcome, compensation or enforcement follow-up is documented, leaving effectiveness uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having documented acceptance, protected facilities and no targeting; lower because this dossier lacks documented traveller enforcement outcomes such as compensation, prosecution or monitored detention placement.

Higher than this dead-letter-statute case: bathroom protection, anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage for gender identity are explicit, with no residual same-sex offence or documented service friction.
Materially higher: no repeated visitor refusals, hostile ejections or unresolved complaints are documented, unlike the recurring service harms and incomplete mediation in that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime shows no universal exposure, organised targeting or birth-sex facility/custody rule, and national protections plus reporting routes are documented in force. Social and legal climate signals are strongly protective, though largely resident-facing and therefore not direct traveller protections. The main limits are evidential: foreign-document practice, hospital and detention placement, care access for minors, and whether remedies change outcomes for trans visitors are undocumented. Non-disaggregated hate-crime counts cannot establish trans-specific risk. Those open questions, rather than any known exposure, hold the rating below the strongest 0.85-0.95 cases.
